--- title: "[Graph.label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Semi-supervised label propagation for node classification. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19060-L19189){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.label_propagation( known_labels, max_iter=100, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Label propagation](/assets/graphs/label-propagation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the edge C to D. Only A (id 1) and G (id 7) are given labels, 0 and 1, shown as badges; every other node adopts the label most common among its neighbors, so the triangle ends with label 0 (accent) and D, E, F, G with label 1 (teal)." width="100%"} Spreads known labels through the network: at each iteration every unlabeled node adopts the most common label among its neighbors (weighted by edge weight). Nodes whose labels are provided in `known_labels=` are held fixed throughout. This is a classic way to classify nodes when only a few of them have known classes: the assumption is that connected nodes tend to share a class (homophily), so labels "flow" from the seeds outward along edges. Typical uses include: - inferring the function of unannotated genes or proteins from annotated interaction partners - spreading a few known spam, fraud, or bot accounts through a social or transaction network - assigning nodes to known groups (e.g., two factions) from a handful of examples Nodes are updated one at a time, and each update immediately influences nodes visited later in the same iteration. Iteration stops early as soon as a full pass changes no label. Votes from neighbors are weighted by the edge `weight` (edges without a weight count as `1.0`). In directed graphs, both incoming and outgoing neighbors vote, so direction is effectively ignored. When two labels receive exactly equal votes, which one wins is arbitrary, so on symmetric graphs (such as a path with a seed at each end) the nodes in the middle may go either way. Unlike community detection with `cmty_louvain()` and friends, this method does not invent groups: every node ends up with one of the seed labels, or `-1` if no seed can reach it. The label assignments are always written to the node DataFrame, even when `return_dict=True`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [known_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `{node_id: label}` dictionary of seed labels. Keys are node IDs (not labels) and values are integers identifying the class. At least one entry is required, and every key must be a node in the graph. Avoid `-1` as a class value since it is used to mark unlabeled nodes. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of propagation iterations (full passes over all nodes). Default is `100`. Propagation usually stops sooner, as soon as a pass changes nothing. In each pass a label can travel many hops, but in large or long, thin graphs a small value may stop propagation before labels have reached every node. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute (node DataFrame column) to store assignments in. If `None` (default), uses `"label_propagation"`. Overwrites the column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return a `{node_id: label}` dictionary directly. If `False` (default), store the result as a node attribute and return `self` for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: label assignments for every node. Seed nodes keep their given labels; nodes that could not be reached from any seed retain label `-1`. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): `self` for chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `known_labels=` is empty or contains a node ID not present in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two dense groups, a triangle "A", "B", "C" and a four-node clique "D" to "G", are joined by the edge "C"-"D". Seeding only "A" with label `0` and "G" with label `1` is enough to classify every node by the group it belongs to: ::: {#888416df .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) g.add_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("D", "F"), ("D", "G"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("F", "G"), ]) seeds = {g.get_id_from_label("A"): 0, g.get_id_from_label("G"): 1} result = g.label_propagation(seeds, return_dict=True) {g.get_label_from_id(nid): lbl for nid, lbl in sorted(result.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 1, 'E': 1, 'F': 1, 'G': 1} ``` ::: ::: Edge weights decide close votes. "Xena" is linked to seed "Alice" (label `0`) with weight `3.0` and to seed "Bob" (label `1`) with weight `1.0`, so she takes Alice's label. A node "Zed" with no connections to any seed keeps `-1`: ::: {#da469fe6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Xena", "Zed"]) g.add_edges([("Xena", "Alice", 3.0), ("Xena", "Bob", 1.0)]) seeds = {g.get_id_from_label("Alice"): 0, g.get_id_from_label("Bob"): 1} result = g.label_propagation(seeds, return_dict=True) {g.get_label_from_id(nid): lbl for nid, lbl in sorted(result.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'Alice': 0, 'Bob': 1, 'Xena': 0, 'Zed': -1} ``` ::: ::: Leaving `return_dict=` at its default stores the labels in the node DataFrame under `attr_name=`, ready for further analysis or for coloring nodes: ::: {#11d3578e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.label_propagation(seeds, attr_name="group").get_node_df().select("label", "group") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

labelgroup
stri64
"Alice"0
"Bob"1
"Xena"0
"Zed"-1
``` ::: :::
